history.name: Commander's Palace
history.shared_categories: American (Traditional), Bars, Breakfast & Brunch, Nightlife, Restaurants

text.text_excerpt: During our 4 month stay in New Orleans, this was our regular place. Being vegan and vegetarian it was the best option in the city, with several other places in the Marigny neighbourhood to wander into if we ever got bored (other veggie food, middle eastern, Japanese). We did not often get bored. Whether we got the BBQ Tofu po-boy, the breakfast burrito, scramble or pizza, we were happy. My only complaints is that the tofu scramble should be scrambled like eggs (my preference at least), not little hard squares, but it was good nonetheless. When we weren't hungry, we went to 13 Monaghan for drinks - good strong mixed ones and Guinness by the pint. On the weekends it's a great place to peopl...

Great staff (if you're not a drunken asshole) and great food (I usually try to order one of the specials, but the regular menu is pretty nice too.) The best part is it's open until 4:30 am (usually) so you can eat there after the seeing some music. They have lots of vegetarian stuff too if you're in to that sort of thing. If you have a group they won't split the check...so be prepared for that. For some reason I also end up ordering lots of Irish coffee here (I sub cream liquer for the usual whip cream.) Oh...and I refuse to order the tater tachos even though everyone raves about them...I'm not sure why, I just won't. Plus there's plenty of other delicious stuff here...

This place is excellent for late night bites and subtle drinks after a good jazz show. It's popular but can be low key compared to the other food joints on the street. I definitely recommend the Tachos! I had loaded Tachos which are tater tots topped with bacon, cheese, sour cream, etc. Tachos are perfect for people who either drank too much or people with the munchies. It's one of those late night bites. These are around $9! I also had their famous frozen Irish coffee which is almost like a caramel frapp but with hints of alcohol. It's truly delicious and will run you $6.50 for a large!
